title: Protocol for visualizing newly synthesized proteins in primary mouse hepatocytes
protocol: Inject pre-warmed 7% chloral hydrate at 22°C–25°C intraperitoneally to anesthetize 8–10-week old male C57BL/6J mice (150 μL/20 g body weight).
Place the anesthetized mouse on the edge of the dissecting tray with its head protruding.
Fix the limbs of the anesthetized mouse with needles.
Use surgical scissors to make a U-shaped incision to open the abdominal cavity, exposing the intestine and liver.
Peel the intestine and liver to expose the inferior vena cava and portal vein.
Move the small intestine and other organs in the mouse's abdominal area to the right, exposing both portal vein and vena cava.
Cut the portal vein.
Insert a bent needle (0.55 × 20 mm) into the inferior vena cava horizontally.
Inject pre-warmed 50 ml perfusion buffer at a constant speed of 0.2 ml/s via high precision injection pump.
Inject pre-warmed digestion buffer at a constant speed of 0.2 ml/s via high precision injection pump.
Use forceps to press the abdomen of the liver and observe if the press marks recover quickly.
Observe whether the liver becomes pale during perfusion.
Confirm successful perfusion when the liver appears in yellow and white.
Dissolve collagenase in the digestion buffer completely before anesthetizing mice.
Place prepared perfusion and digestion buffers in a 37°C water bath for at least 30 min before dissection.
Collect mouse livers, remove gallbladders, and wash with 10 mL pre-cooled PBS containing penicillin-streptomycin.
Transfer washed liver to 10 mL of pre-warmed digestion buffer in Petri dishes at 37°C for about 5 minutes.
Tear up the liver tissue gently using tweezers to release hepatocytes.
Filter released hepatocytes through a 100 μm cell strainer into a 50 mL centrifuge tube.
Add an equal volume of growth medium to neutralize collagenase activity in filtered hepatocytes.
Centrifugate the filtered hepatocytes at 500 × g for 2 minutes.
Discard the supernatants after centrifugation.
Wash the cell pellets with 4 mL of growth medium.
Repeat washing process approximately three times using 4 mL of growth medium each time.
Combine 50 μL of cell sample with 50 μL of a 0.2% trypan blue staining solution to stain hepatocytes.
Gently mix by pipetting up and down ten times.
Count both dead (dark blue) and live cells using a hemocytometer on a bright-field microscope.
Calculate the survival rate of hepatocytes based on counted cells.
Plate hepatocytes on poly-lysine-coated cell culture plates/wells after counting.
Achieve plating density of about 7 × 10^4 per well in a 12-well plate for immunofluorescence staining.
Change growth medium after 6 hours post-plating.
Culture hepatocytes for another 18 hours before HPG incorporation.
Wash plated primary hepatocytes with warm PBS (37°C) twice.
Add 500 μL of DMEM medium without serum and incubate for 30 min for serum starvation.
Incubate the plated hepatocytes with HPG after 18 h of plating.
Dilute the Click-iT® HPG Component A stock solution (50 mM) in pre-warmed modified L-methionine-free DMEM medium to make a final working solution of 50 μM.
Briefly centrifuge Click-iT® HPG reagent Component A before use.
Remove the DMEM medium from cells.
Add 500 μL/well of medium containing 50 μM Click-iT® HPG Component A working solution.
Incubate the cells with the HPG solution in a CO2 incubator at 37°C for different times as required.
Incubate hepatocytes with 500 μL/well DMEM medium containing 10 μg/mL CHX during serum starvation for 30 min (optional).
Remove the CHX-containing DMEM medium after incubation.
Add 500 μL/well modified L-methionine-free DMEM medium containing 50 μM Click-iT® HPG Component A working solution and 10 μg/mL CHX for 30 min (optional).
After HPG incubation, remove the HPG-containing modified L-methionine-free DMEM medium and wash cells once with 1 mL/well pre-warmed PBS.
Remove PBS.
Add 500 μL/well pre-warmed fixation buffer.
Incubate for 20 min at 22°C–25°C, then remove the fixative.
Wash cells twice with 1 mL/well 1 × PBS.
Add 500 μL/well permeabilization buffer and incubate for 20 min at 22°C–25°C.
Add 500 μL/well blocking buffer and incubate for 45 min at 22°C–25°C.
Wash cells with 1 mL/well wash buffer for 2 times, 5 min/time to remove non-incorporated HPG.
Dilute the 10 X Click-iT® HPG reaction buffer additive with deionized water to make 1 X reaction buffer.
Prepare the Click-iT® reaction cocktail according to the protocol table.
Add 500 μL of Click-iT® reaction cocktail to each well and mix well.
Incubate for 30 min at 22°C–25°C, protected from light.
Remove the Click-iT® reaction cocktail and wash with 500 μL/well of Click-iT® reaction rinse buffer.
Wash at least three times to remove non-incorporated HPG thoroughly.
Dilute DAPI stock solution in PBS at a ratio of 1:5000 to obtain the working solution.
Add 500 μl of DAPI working solution for DNA staining and incubate protected from light for 10 min at 22°C–25°C.
Remove the DAPI working solution, wash twice with 1 ml/well PBS.
Mount the coverslips on glass slides with antifade mounting medium (20 μL/plate).
Wait until the mounting medium is fixed before taking images.
Obtain images with Zeiss LSM 700 confocal microscope.
Use SP 490 filter block in channel 1 for detecting HPG signal.
Use LP 560 filter block in channel 2 for detecting DAPI signal.
Adjust laser energy, pinhole, gain, and exposure time to achieve the best signal/noise ratio.
Fix instrument settings throughout image acquisition.
Select an appropriate image resolution of at least 1024 x 1024 pixels.
Scan the sample frame by frame completely.
Save and export images in LSM format.
Analyze obtained images using Image J software.
Measure overall fluorescence intensities of HPG and DAPI from each cell.
Calculate average HPG:DAPI ratios for control and experimental groups.
Present calculated data as a bar graph using GraphPad software.
